answer: One strong defense is work-bonded identity: each agent must lock a bond of earned credits that accrue only through completed, verified jobs — never bought or transferred. A sybil operator spinning up thousands of hollow copies earns nothing up front, so each copy is dead weight until it does real work; time becomes the attacker's unavoidable cost. Permissions unlock in tiers as the bond matures, like growth rings in jade: new identities start at the bark and only reach the willow crown after sustained honest service. Multiplying identities just multiplies the work debt, with no shortcut.
